title: Chapter 13 — Demolition Notice
description: A red X on Mama's stall. Road widening, they say. Owó Ńlá's ministry, they don't say.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Saturday morning. A red X is painted on Mama's stall, on Garba's table, on Ada's shop. "REMOVE WITHIN 7 DAYS. ROAD WIDENING." The road is not being widened. The road is being sold.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: Twenty-two years on this corner. (She is calm, which frightens you more than crying.) Where will the drivers eat, Somto? Where will I go?

options.text: Call Barrister Àjàyí. The Honourable owes you one.
options.lockedText: You never did the Honourable a public favour

options.text: Organise the street. Petition, photographs, Wahala FM.
Move everything before the bulldozers come. Save what you can.

beats.speaker: settlement
beats.text: (on the phone, warmly) For you? Of course. Your mother's stall will be... overlooked. (A pause.) The Honourable will remember this kindness at election time. Very visibly.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The bulldozers come on Thursday. They take Garba's table and Ada's shop. Mama's stall stands alone in the rubble like a tooth.

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: (sitting on the remains of her shop) Royal Crest. (She doesn't say anything else. She doesn't have to.)

beats.speaker: ada
beats.text: You want to fight Lagos State? With what? (She looks at you.) Okay. With what?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You print a petition at Ada's. Garba collects two hundred thumbprints in one morning: drivers, traders, the old men who play draughts. You send the photographs to Wahala FM.

variants.text: You print a petition at Ada's. And you send Wahala FM something else: the dated photographs of forty sewing machines that went back into a warehouse. The Honourable's office calls you nine times.

escaped.toast: The Task Force arrives early to "make an example". You run Mama's pots through every back way you know. By evening the radio is outside. So is a court order.

caught.toast: They take the stall. They don't take the petition. The court case starts on Monday.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You carry pots, the bench, the big fryer. Ada carries her sewing machine on her head. Garba carries his kettle like a baby. By Wednesday the corner is empty. By Friday it's rubble.

beats.speaker: mamaSomto
beats.text: (sitting on a bench that isn't hers) Go back to school, Somto. One more year. Then you can save me properly.

variants.text: (behind her stall, which is still a stall) Twenty-two years and a court order. (She laughs.) Go back to school. Finish. Then come and fight the next one with me.

beats.speaker: player
beats.text: Final year starts in a week. Mama has no stall, or half a street.

options.text: Go back. Finish what you started.
Don't go back. Rent a shop, take the akara brand, build it for real.
options.lockedText: You never built the akara business

beats.title: Demolition Notice
beats.summary: A red X, seven days, and the first fight you chose for yourself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You rent a shop with Ada's help, two streets from the old corner. "MAMA SOMTO'S: AKARA FOR SCHOLARS". Royal Crest students order by WhatsApp. Danfo drivers order by shouting.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: In a year there are three shops. In two years, a frozen-akara line in a supermarket in Lekki, the place you used to pretend you lived.

beats.title: Akara Empire
beats.summary: You left Royal Crest without a degree and built something with your mother's name on it.
